One planet built for the private and the internal, running at its classical worst. One planet built for the public and the performed, running at its classical best. Same nine-minute window, 15 March 1993, Mumbai.

Nothing here explains her career. It's just an unusually sharp contrast to build a reading around — and her birth time is solid enough that we can actually show you the houses too.

What's public

Being Mahesh Bhatt and Soni Razdan's daughter has followed her since Student of the Year. It resurfaced hard in 2020, when Bollywood's industry-wide nepotism debate blew up after Sushant Singh Rajput's death.

She's addressed it directly more than once — acknowledging the head start while pointing at more than a decade of work since.

Her Rahu sits in Scorpio, conjunct her Moon, in the 11th house — public reach and networks. Rahu amplifies whatever it touches, and here it's sitting directly on the planet of image.

A chart built for getting looked at more than most, for better and worse.

🎤 The interview clip that wouldn't die

A 2015 TV quiz-show clip where she stumbled on the President of India's name went viral and turned into a years-long meme. She's since spoken openly about how much it stung at the time.

Actually learn this

Astrology, but make it make sense

Zero background needed. Read this once and you can decode the chart above yourself — no astrologer required.

LESSON 01

What a birth chart even is

It's a photo of the sky from the exact spot and second you were born — where every planet was sitting, frozen.

Vedic astrology reads that snapshot as raw material, not a script. What anyone does with a placement is still entirely up to them.

Hers: 15 March 1993, 04:10 AM, Mumbai. That sky had a debilitated Moon in Scorpio and an exalted Venus in Pisces one sign apart from a cluster of retrograde planets — an unusually loaded chart either way you read it.
LESSON 02

LESSON 03

Why "which sign" actually matters

Every planet has signs where it's comfortable and signs where it struggles. Same planet, wildly different output.

  • Own sign (★ home) — the planet owns the place. Full strength.
  • Exalted (★ strongest) — its single best sign. Peak output, no friction.
  • Debilitated (↓ weakest) — its single worst sign. Still works, just against constant resistance.
Her scorecard: one planet at each classical extreme — Saturn on home ground, Venus at its single strongest sign, Moon at its single weakest. Most charts don't hit all three flavours at once. Hers does.
LESSON 04

Dashas — why timing is the whole game

Your life splits into long stretches, each one run by a single planet. Fixed order, fixed lengths, and which one you start in is decided by exactly where the Moon was at birth. The technical name is dasha.

Her ladder, computed:
Mercury 1993–95 · Ketu 1995–2002 · Venus 2002–2022 · Sun 2022–2028 (current) · Moon 2028–2038

Twenty years of Venus covers essentially her entire rise — debut to marriage. Sun has run everything since.
LESSON 05

Sub-periods — the chapters inside the chapter

A twenty-year stretch is too blunt to be useful on its own, so each mahadasha splits into shorter sub-periods (antardashas), each briefly handed to a different planet.

Right now: she's in a Sun–Saturn antardasha, running 29 October 2025 to 11 October 2026. We're showing you this one because it's the current, verified sub-period — we haven't recomputed her full historical antardasha ladder back through 1993, so we're not backdating sub-periods we haven't actually run.
LESSON 06

What a verified birth time actually buys you

A chart has two layers: the signs, which barely move across a whole day, and the houses — plus the rising sign, the lagna — which shift roughly every two hours and need the birth minute to place correctly.

Alia Bhatt's birth time — 04:10 AM, Mumbai — comes from the Seth astrological databank with a Rodden rating of A ("good": a documented, reasonably reliable source, not a guess). That's an uncommon level of confidence for a Bollywood chart.

What that unlocks: a rising sign (Capricorn), house placements for all nine grahas, and an actual answer to the manglik question — three things this site deliberately withholds on charts with disputed or missing birth times. We still name the source and rating every time, because "verified" is a confidence level, not a certainty.
LESSON 07

So — is Alia Bhatt manglik?

The most-searched astrology question about almost anyone — and for once, the birth time holds up well enough to actually answer it.

"Manglik" (Kuja dosha) means Mars sits in one of a handful of houses tied to marriage, counted two different ways depending on the classical method.

Counted from her rising sign (Capricorn): Mars sits in the 6th house — not a manglik house. By that method, not manglik.

Counted from her Moon (Scorpio) instead: Mars lands in the 8th house — which is one. By that method, manglik (specifically "Chandra-manglik," the moon-based version some traditions treat as milder).

Different schools weight the two methods differently, and neither classical cancellation we check for (Mars own/exalted, or a Jupiter aspect on Mars) applies here. We're giving you both readings rather than picking whichever sounds more definitive. What's not in dispute: she's been married to Ranbir Kapoor since April 2022.
LESSON 08

How to actually read that chart square

The grid earlier on this page is a South-Indian chart — the easiest of the three styles to learn, because the signs never move.

Twelve boxes around the edge, one per zodiac sign, always in the same places. Pisces top-left, then clockwise: Aries, Taurus, Gemini along the top, Cancer and Leo down the right, and so on.

Try it: find the box marked PIS. Two symbols sit in it — her Sun and her exalted Venus, conjunct. You just read a kundli.
LESSON 09

Aspects — planets shouting across the chart

A planet doesn't only affect the box it sits in — it also throws influence at other boxes from a distance. Astrologers call this an aspect. The basic rule: every planet aspects the box directly opposite it. Saturn, Mars, Jupiter and the nodes get extra reach on top of that.

Hers: Saturn's special aspects reach three, seven and ten houses ahead of itself. From her 2nd house, that lands on the 4th, 8th and 11th. The 11th is exactly where her Moon and Rahu sit — the steadying, patient planet currently running her life is aimed straight at her weakest placement.
LESSON 10

Retrograde and combust, without the drama

Retrograde means the planet appeared to move backwards across the sky — an optical effect of Earth overtaking it, not an actual reversal. The classical reading is that the planet's themes turn more internal and slower to show results.

Hers: three of her five non-luminary, non-node planets — Mercury, Jupiter and Venus — are all retrograde at once. That's an unusual concentration. Classical astrology doesn't read this as bad; if anything, a retrograde planet is said to work with unusual intensity once it delivers, just on its own schedule rather than an obvious one.
LESSON 11

What this can and can't tell you

  • It can describe tendencies and time long stretches — that part is arithmetic, and two astrologers with the same birth data compute the same periods.
  • It can't tell you what someone does with those tendencies. Two near-identical charts live completely different lives.
  • It definitely can't give exact dates for a diagnosis, a divorce, or an exam result — and anyone who does is guessing with confidence.
The honest framing: a chart describes the raw material and the weather. It is not a script, and nothing on this page should be read as one.
